items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: I had Roy Palmer on the trombone.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Who else was in that band, Tudi Tootie? Your Chicago band.
I had Roy Palmer on the trombone.
Hard. That one rocked right in. Yeah.
Do you know Roy Palmer? I never met him.
I used to try to imitate him when I had a trombone. But I couldn't tell him. Because you didn't hear that. Not Roy Palmer. He was too old. Willie Carnish? I knew you didn't know about him.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: I brought Sugar Johnny, trumpet, Louis Keppert on guitar, Roy Palmer on trombone, Herbert Lindsay on violin, and a boy named Lawrence Duell on clarinet, myself on bass.

ctx.x: No. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. She's a white girl. She used to clunk band. You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing. She used to be in a bale of cotton. She was blackface. When you get on the stage, that bale of cotton was out there. They couldn't go out. We'd be all lying around in this cotton, see, with a couple of holes on, satin cover holes, different colors, and bandana, hangers, and hats. So I had, when we started playing, this fave of cotton opened up. And…
